title: Make layout and component slicing Unicode-width and grapheme aware
description:
## Evidence

- Pippa visible_width explicitly says every character counts as 1 and no wide-character handling is performed in src/layout.mbt:50-59. truncate, padding, table cells, viewport, text_input, and textarea build on character counts.
- Bubbles/Bubble Tea use ansi.StringWidth, lipgloss.Width, runewidth, and uniseg across renderer, viewport, table, textinput, and textarea. Bubbles tests include Chinese placeholder, wide viewport content, and emoji insertion.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Add or run a layout assertion such as assert_eq(visible_width("界"), 2).
2. Add or run a truncation assertion that cuts mixed-width text by terminal cells, for example a CJK character followed by ASCII.
3. Exercise table/viewport/text input rendering with CJK, emoji, or combining marks.

Current result: the implementation counts each MoonBit Char as width 1, so wide CJK, emoji, combining marks, and grapheme clusters report the wrong terminal cell width and can be truncated or cursor-positioned incorrectly.

## Expected

Layout helpers and components use terminal cell width and grapheme clusters rather than raw codepoint count.
acceptance_criteria: Width, truncation, padding, cursor movement, viewport slicing, table cells, text input, and textarea use terminal cell width and grapheme clusters rather than raw codepoint count. Tests cover CJK wide characters, emoji, combining marks, ANSI-styled text, and mixed-width truncation without splitting graphemes or leaking styles.

title: Prevent stale timer and stopwatch ticks after pause/reset/restart
description:
## Evidence

- Pippa timer and stopwatch schedule plain Tick messages with Cmd::after(interval_ms) and no component ID or generation tag in src/component/timer.mbt and src/component/stopwatch.mbt.
- Bubbles timer/stopwatch messages carry ID and tag fields; Update rejects messages from other instances or stale generations to avoid ticking too fast.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a Pippa timer or stopwatch with interval_ms = 100, which schedules Tick A.
2. Pause before Tick A fires.
3. Start again before Tick A is delivered, which schedules Tick B.
4. Let Tick A arrive while running is true again.

Likely result: Tick A advances the component early and can schedule another tick, so the component cadence can become faster than intended. Multiple embedded timers/stopwatches have the same risk if parent routing sends a Tick to the wrong component.

## Expected

Ticks from an old paused/reset generation, or from another component instance, are ignored.
acceptance_criteria: Add red tests for pause/restart stale ticks and multiple timers/stopwatches receiving each other messages. Fix uses IDs, generation tags, cancellation tokens, or another explicit ownership scheme so stale ticks are ignored. Timer timeout and stopwatch elapsed behavior remain stable under normal cadence.

title: Close text_input and textarea behavioral gaps
description:
Evidence:
- Pippa TextInputModel is value/cursor/placeholder/focused with single-char insert/delete and edge cursor movement in src/component/text_input.mbt. Pippa TextareaModel supports plain value, cursor row/col, width/height, scroll offsets, placeholder, and focus in src/component/textarea.mbt.
- Bubbles textinput has prompt, echo modes, char limit, validation errors, width viewporting, suggestions, paste command, word movement/deletion, configurable keymap, cursor model/style, and sanitization. Bubbles textarea has prompt/prompt func, line numbers, char/max width/max height/max content limits, dynamic height, soft wrapping, viewport integration, cursor model/style, sanitization, paste, word operations, and much broader tests including emoji.

Gap: Pippa text editing is useful but too small for password fields, validation, suggestions/autocomplete, rich cursor behavior, paste, word editing, dynamic multi-line editing, and robust international text.
acceptance_criteria: Text input covers prompt, width viewporting, char limit, validation error state, echo password/none, suggestions navigation/acceptance, paste, word movement/deletion, configurable keymap, and cursor mode/style hooks. Textarea covers line numbers/prompt hooks, dynamic height, soft wrap, max content/width/height limits, paste, word operations, vertical navigation memory, and Unicode/grapheme-safe editing. Tests include emoji, CJK/wide characters, paste, validation, suggestions, and dynamic height.

title: Expose lifecycle results, quit/interrupt/suspend, and external exec support
description:
Evidence:
- Pippa Program::run returns Unit and exits through should_quit/catch_interrupt plus ProgramHandle::send/release_terminal/restore_terminal in src/program.mbt.
- Bubble Tea v2 exposes Quit/Interrupt/Suspend/Resume messages in tea.go:555-590, context/signal/panic/renderer options in options.go, run errors such as ErrProgramKilled/ErrInterrupted/ErrProgramPanic in tea.go, and Exec/ExecProcess in exec.go to restore the terminal around external commands.

Gap: Pippa cannot report the final model/error from run, cannot model quit/interrupt/suspend/resume as first-class messages, and has no built-in process exec command that temporarily releases the terminal.
acceptance_criteria: Program run APIs expose a result shape suitable for tests and callers. Built-in Quit, Interrupt, Suspend, and Resume flows are deliverable through update. A command can run an external process while terminal state is released/restored. Cancellation/signal/panic-like cleanup paths restore terminal modes and are covered by native tests.

title: Add terminal query/effect commands and response messages
description:
Evidence:
- Pippa Cmd currently exposes none/msg/perform/tick/after/batch/sequence/map in src/command.mbt, plus raw ANSI helpers in src/ansi.mbt.
- Bubble Tea exposes Every/Tick/RequestWindowSize in commands.go, ClearScreen and ModeReportMsg in screen.go, RequestCapability/CapabilityMsg in termcap.go, terminal color requests in color.go, clipboard OSC52 commands in clipboard.go, RequestCursorPosition in cursor.go, RequestTerminalVersion in xterm.go, and Raw in raw.go.

Gap: Pippa has useful timers and ANSI strings, but not typed runtime effects for terminal queries/replies and not a system-clock-aligned Every command.
acceptance_criteria: Pippa has typed command constructors and response messages for window size request, clear screen, terminal capabilities, terminal/cursor colors, cursor position, terminal version, clipboard read/write where supported, raw query escape payloads, and system-clock-aligned Every. Parser/runtime tests prove query replies can be injected and delivered as typed messages.

title: Expand input parsing to typed UTF-8, key, mouse, paste, and terminal replies
description:
Evidence:
- Pippa KeyMsg is Char/Special(String)/Modified(String,String) in src/message.mbt and parse_input only treats bytes 0x20..0x7e as printable ASCII in src/input.mbt:137. The CSI parser handles a small set of arrows/page/home/end/focus/paste and X10 mouse. MouseMsg loses button identity, modifiers, wheel events, and SGR coordinates.
- Bubble Tea v2 key.go models KeyPressMsg/KeyReleaseMsg with Text, Mod, Code, ShiftedCode, BaseCode, and IsRepeat. mouse.go models click/release/wheel/motion with button and modifiers. keyboard.go has KeyboardEnhancementsMsg, paste.go has paste start/end/content messages, and the runtime parses many terminal reply events.

Gap: non-ASCII text entry, modern keyboard protocol events, wheel/mouse modifiers, paste boundaries, and terminal reply events are either unknown bytes or lossy string events in Pippa.
acceptance_criteria: InputEvent/KeyMsg/MouseMsg evolve to preserve printable UTF-8 text, typed special key codes, modifiers in canonical order, key release/repeat/enhancement metadata where available, SGR mouse coordinates with buttons/wheel/modifiers, paste start/end/content, and terminal query replies. Tests cover UTF-8 characters, wide characters, SGR wheel/click, modifier combinations, bracketed paste boundaries, and unknown-but-well-formed escape sequences.

title: Add Bubble Tea v2-style View surface for per-render terminal state
description:
Evidence:
- Pippa public Program.view is (Model) -> String and terminal modes are program-level booleans in src/program.mbt and src/pkg.generated.mbti.
- Bubble Tea v2 View carries Content, OnMouse, Cursor, BackgroundColor, ForegroundColor, WindowTitle, ProgressBar, AltScreen, ReportFocus, DisableBracketedPasteMode, MouseMode, and KeyboardEnhancements in /mnt/data/Code/bubbletea/tea.go:84-189.

Gap: Pippa apps cannot return structured per-render terminal state, cursor state, terminal title/colors/progress, or view-scoped mouse behavior without manual escape strings and side channels.
acceptance_criteria: Existing string views remain ergonomic. A public View or equivalent can represent content plus cursor, title, terminal colors, progress, mouse mode or handler, focus/paste/alt-screen hints, and keyboard enhancement requests. The runtime applies, diffs, and cleans up those fields with tests that use injected output/raw input rather than visual inspection.

title: Bubble Tea/Bubbles parity roadmap for Pippa
description:
Current-state comparison target:
- Pippa: /mnt/data/Code/pippa on main (after repo-local beads init).
- Bubble Tea: /mnt/data/Code/bubbletea at c60f0c5, including v2 runtime files such as commands.go, tea.go, options.go, key.go, mouse.go, screen.go, termcap.go, color.go, clipboard.go, cursor.go.
- Bubbles: /mnt/data/Code/bubbles at 8585ef8, with packages cursor, filepicker, help, key, list, paginator, progress, spinner, stopwatch, table, textarea, textinput, timer, viewport.

Purpose: track the concrete missing features, incongruities, and bug-shaped parity gaps for a MoonBit TUI framework that keeps engine and bundled components in one repo.
acceptance_criteria: A first-pass child bead set exists for runtime/view state, terminal effects/query messages, input/key/mouse parsing, lifecycle/process behavior, key/help models, text editing components, list, table/viewport, filepicker, timer/stopwatch identity, Unicode width, and lower-priority component polish. Each child bead cites current Pippa and Bubble Tea/Bubbles evidence.

title: Build a parity example suite from Bubble Tea and Bubbles scenarios
description:
Evidence:
- Bubble Tea examples include simple, sequence, window-size, focus-blur, keyboard-enhancements, mouse/clickable, file-picker, help, list-default/fancy/simple, pager, paginator, progress variants, spinner/spinners, stopwatch, suspend, table/table-resize, tabs, textarea/textinput/textinputs, timer, set-window-title/color, query-term, pipe, exec, and more.
- Pippa currently has hello and showcase examples.

Gap: without examples that map the upstream scenarios to Pippa idioms, it is hard to validate API ergonomics and find missing seams early.
acceptance_criteria: Add an examples/parity area or documented checklist that covers representative runtime, input, terminal query, and component scenarios. Each example should be small, runnable with moon, and tied to a feature bead when blocked by missing API. The suite should avoid pure visual snapshot churn where behavior can be asserted directly.

title: Fill filepicker metadata, history, symlink, and auto-height gaps
description:
Evidence:
- Pippa FileEntry stores name/path/is_dir and FilepickerModel covers current_directory, entries, cursor, selected_path, height, hidden toggle, file/directory selection flags, allowed extensions, loading scan handle, and error in src/component/filepicker.mbt.
- Bubbles filepicker has AllowedTypes, KeyMap, ShowPermissions, ShowSize, ShowHidden, DirAllowed/FileAllowed, FileSelected, selected/min/max stacks for navigation history, AutoHeight, Cursor string, Styles, hidden detection per OS, and display of permissions/size/symlink/disabled states.

Gap: Pippa has the important nonblocking scanner, but lacks metadata display/control, per-OS hidden semantics beyond dotfiles, symlink/permissions/size awareness, directory view stack restoration, auto height, and keymap/style customization.
acceptance_criteria: File entries carry enough metadata for symlink, permissions, size, and disabled state. Hidden-file behavior is platform-aware. Directory navigation restores previous selection/window when going back. Auto-height and keymap/style customization are available. Tests cover large directory scan continuation, metadata filtering/rendering, back-stack restoration, and allowed type behavior.

title: Make table viewport-backed with focus, keymap, paging, and width/height controls
description:
Evidence:
- Pippa table.mbt exposes columns, rows, cursor, selected, CursorUp/CursorDown/Select/SetRows, and renders every row with fixed column widths.
- Bubbles table uses a viewport internally, has focus state, default/custom KeyMap, help model, styles, height/width options, page/half-page/top/bottom navigation, SetColumns/SetRows/SetWidth/SetHeight methods, and tests around ANSI-width row rendering and responsive widths.

Gap: Pippa tables cannot be focused/blurred, cannot page through large row sets, do not expose keymaps/help, have no viewport clipping, and have weak width/height controls.
acceptance_criteria: Table supports focus, configurable keymap/help, viewport-backed height/width clipping, page/half-page/top/bottom navigation, column and row setters, selection/cursor helpers, ANSI/Unicode width-aware cell rendering, and tests for large tables and resized widths.

title: Upgrade list into delegated fuzzy list component
description:
Evidence:
- Pippa list.mbt stores Array[String], uses case-insensitive substring filtering, and renders a simple paged list.
- Bubbles list has Item and ItemDelegate abstractions, fuzzy ranked filtering with match indexes, filter states, async FilterMatchesMsg, status messages with lifetime, title/filter/status/pagination/help toggles, spinner integration, paginator/help/textinput composition, infinite scrolling, custom item names, and additional help bindings.

Gap: Pippa cannot represent structured list items, custom item render/update behavior, ranked fuzzy matching, match highlighting metadata, status messages, or a full-featured list browser.
acceptance_criteria: List supports item values beyond String, delegate rendering/update hooks, fuzzy ranked filtering with matched indexes, explicit filter states, configurable keymap/help, optional title/filter/status/pagination sections, status messages with expiry, infinite scrolling, and tests for selection stability across filtering and item updates.

title: Expand viewport with horizontal scrolling, soft wrap, gutters, highlights, and mouse wheel
description:
Evidence:
- Pippa viewport.mbt has content, width, height, vertical offset, total_lines, vertical scroll/page/top/bottom, SetContent, and Resize.
- Bubbles viewport has horizontal xOffset, configurable horizontal step, SoftWrap, FillHeight, MouseWheelEnabled/Delta, YPosition for rendering, Style, LeftGutterFunc, line styling, highlights with selected navigation, ScrollPercent/AtTop/AtBottom/PastBottom helpers, and extensive ANSI/wide-character tests.

Gap: Pippa viewport is vertical-only and cannot handle horizontal navigation, soft wrap, mouse wheel input, gutters/line numbers, highlighted ranges, or useful scroll state helpers.
acceptance_criteria: Viewport supports horizontal scroll, soft wrap, fill-height, mouse wheel messages, gutter callbacks, highlight ranges and navigation, scroll percent/top/bottom helpers, style hooks, and Unicode/ANSI-width-aware rendering tests.

title: Introduce configurable keymap and help components
description:
Evidence:
- Pippa key.mbt has a flat Binding {keys, help}, fixed helper constructors, matches(), and help_view() over a flat binding list. Components expose domain-specific Msg enums but no reusable KeyMap surface.
- Bubbles key.Binding supports configurable keys, help key/description, enabled/disabled state, unbind, and Matches. Bubbles help.Model renders short/full grouped help, skips disabled bindings, and truncates by width. Many Bubbles components expose KeyMap structs that satisfy help.KeyMap.

Gap: Pippa users must hand-wire input to component messages and cannot easily customize bindings, disable commands, or render width-aware generated help for components.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable key binding API supports keys, help key/description, enabled state, unbind, mutation/copy semantics appropriate for MoonBit, and matching against Pippa key events. A help component renders short and full grouped help with width truncation. Components either expose default KeyMap values or a clear adapter layer from InputEvent to component Msg.

title: Add spinner/progress presets and behavioral configuration
description:
Evidence:
- Pippa spinner has a fixed frame set/label and Tick message. Pippa progress_bar has width, percentage toggle, color blend, empty color, and spring options.
- Bubbles spinner exposes many named presets with FPS and style. Bubbles progress exposes fill characters, default blend/colors/color function, percentage formatting/style, width setters, spring options, scaled mode, frame messages, and helpers.

Gap: this is mostly polish/configuration rather than core runtime, but parity users will expect reusable spinner presets and progress behavior knobs.
acceptance_criteria: Spinner supports named presets, frame interval/FPS, style hooks, and safe tick identity if needed. Progress supports custom fill/empty characters, color function or palette, percentage format/style, scaled mode, width setters, and tests for animation convergence and rendering options.
